title: Push and pop on a linked stack
summary: Last in, first out. Both operations touch only the top node, so both are O(1).

checkpoints.text: The stack is an object in `main`. Its only member is `topNode`, which is NULL: the stack is empty.
Pushing 15. The new node points down at the old top (5), and `topNode` moves up to it. These are the same two lines as inserting at the front of a list.
`peek` reads the top value without removing it: 25. The last value pushed is the first one you can reach.
Popping. `topNode` moves down to the node below before the old top is deleted.
The old top (25) is freed. Its value was copied into `value` first, because a deleted node must not be read.

checkpoints.at: cout << "The stack is empty again" << endl;
checkpoints.text: Popped 25, 15, then 5: the reverse of the order they were pushed. Every node was deleted by `pop`, so nothing leaked.
